v: Classic Luv Ranjan territory with a fresher pair and even more entertainment — the first half takes time, but the interval, second half and gloriously mad climax make it a very good watch.
e: Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar follows Luv Ranjan’s familiar relationship-comedy template, but Ranbir Kapoor and Shraddha Kapoor bring fresh chemistry and the film finds its strongest rhythm after the interval. The crazy climax is exactly the kind of comic escape that makes the whole conflict work without over-explaining it.
body:
If you enjoy Luv Ranjan’s style of films, Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar is another easy recommendation.

It follows the familiar Luv Ranjan template — fast dialogue, relationship confusion, exaggerated emotional logic and comedy built around modern romance.

So yes, bits and pieces may remind you of his earlier movies.

But for me, this one has much more entertainment value 👌

The first half does the necessary setup, although I felt it could have been tighter and funnier.

The real strengths are the interval block, the second half and that absolutely crazy climax.

Ranbir Kapoor and Shraddha Kapoor make a fresh onscreen pair and their chemistry works very well. Both are completely comfortable with the film’s energetic dialogue-heavy tone.

The die-hard Luv Ranjan fan in me still missed the old combination of Kartik Aaryan and Nushrratt Bharuccha, because I kept imagining how naturally they might have fitted into this world 😄

So their guest appearances were a very pleasant surprise.

The supporting cast is uniformly good, and Dimple Kapadia once again gets a memorable part and has great fun with it.

My favourite decision is the climax.

I kept wondering how the director would resolve the central conflict without making one side look completely wrong.

Instead of getting trapped in heavy justification, he simply chooses madness — and turns the finale into a laugh riot 🤣

By that point you are enjoying the chaos too much to demand a courtroom-style explanation.

Overall, Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar is a very good watch — especially if Luv Ranjan’s brand of relationship comedy already works for you.

v: SRK’s comeback is a full-blown big-screen celebration — swagger, action, BGM, glamour, twists and Salman-sized madness packed into one wildly entertaining spy spectacle.
e: Pathaan worked for me as exactly the comeback vehicle Shah Rukh Khan needed: unapologetically large, stylish and crowd-pleasing. The film may not be technically flawless, but its cast, action, terrific BGM and Spy Universe ambition make those imperfections very easy to ignore.
body:
EXCELLENT TREAT!!!!! 😍

I walked out of Pathaan still completely charged by the experience, and this is absolutely the kind of film I could watch multiple times.

Hindi cinema had been going through a difficult theatrical phase, with several big films failing to connect and dubbed releases taking an increasingly large share of the box office.

And then, after four years away from a full-fledged starring vehicle, Shah Rukh Khan returned with exactly the kind of larger-than-life movie his fans were waiting for.

And of course, Bhai Jaan turns up to add his own helping hand to the madness 🙏🤣

Pathaan has enough story and emotion to support its spectacle, while the cast throws itself fully into the action.

SRK has the swagger, Deepika Padukone is terrific in both the action and glamour portions, and John Abraham gets the presence needed for a proper big-screen antagonist.

Technically, the film is not perfect.

But the pace, scale and entertainment are strong enough that I simply did not care about every imperfection while watching it.

The BGM is terrific, the production values are suitably huge, and the action keeps trying to go bigger.

Most importantly, this feels like a perfect comeback film for SRK.

A neutral audience can enjoy the spectacle; a die-hard Shah Rukh fan will probably spend half the runtime screaming 😍

I also liked how Pathaan expands the YRF Spy Universe. In the same way a major crossover film can suddenly make separate characters feel part of one larger world, this movie makes the future possibilities of the franchise much more exciting.

To put the experience in one very simple filmi checklist:

Content? Irukuuu!!!
Character arcs? Irukuuu!!!
Emotion? Irukuuu!!!
Twists? Irukuuu!!!
Grand visuals? Irukuuu!!!
Action? Irukuuu!!!
BGM? Irukuuu!!!
Songs? Irukuuu!!!
Hotness? Irukuuu!!!

And when you want complete physics-defying BANG BANG?

Salman Khan Irukuuu!!! 🤣🔥

For me, Pathaan is pure big-screen entertainment and one of those star vehicles that understands exactly what its audience came to celebrate.

v: Poonakalu raaledhu… kaani time-pass ayipoyindi 😄 Routine story, ordinary music and a weak final stretch, but vintage Chiru comedy, dialect and dances make it a decent one-time watch.
e: Waltair Veerayya is formula cinema with limited story impact, but Bobby understands the nostalgic Chiranjeevi flavour his audience wants. The Srikakulam dialect, comedy timing and dance staging bring flashes of vintage Chiru even though the Ravi Teja track and climax never deliver the expected high.
body:
Poonakalu raaledhu… kaani time-pass ayipoyindi 😄

Bobby, a self-proclaimed Chiranjeevi fan, clearly wanted to present Chiru in the massy, comic avatar that helped make him the Mega Star.

On that front, Waltair Veerayya gives fans plenty of nostalgic moments.

The main drawbacks are the lack of truly impactful content and the fact that Chiru’s look in a few portions does not carry the same effortless grace we remember from his peak years.

The story itself is ordinary and the screenplay follows a very familiar commercial formula.

But it has been a long time since Chiranjeevi played this kind of character, and that alone makes the film reasonably entertaining for a normal viewer while giving long-time fans a stronger vintage kick.

I personally got flashes of Annayya, Shankar Dada and Andarivaadu from the massy presentation, Srikakulam dialect and especially the comedy timing.

And that proves something important: whatever changes age may bring visually, Chiru’s comic timing is still very much intact.

If a director gives him a genuinely funny out-and-out entertainer, I still believe he can do wonders 🙏

The little Jambalakadi Jaaru Mitaya bit is a perfect example of that old-school ease 👌

The songs and BGM are pretty ordinary for me and do not add much impact.

The dances, however, are deliberately choreographed to bring back that vintage Chiru feeling, and those portions work.

The bigger disappointment comes in the second half.

The heavily hyped combination with Ravi Teja never gives me the expected Poonakalu. I wanted much more from that track than a fairly routine backstory.

The pre-climax and climax also try to do something different, but those ideas never gel properly with the rest of the film.

Overall, Waltair Veerayya is a one-time watch with routine direction and not-so-great content.

But as a Chiranjeevi film after his comeback, it is still a considerably better and more enjoyable outing than several of the films around it.

v: Plenty of Balayya elevation, but very little fresh content beneath it — hardcore fans may enjoy the punches, yet the recycled dual-role template and repetitive action make this far less impactful than Akhanda, Simha or Legend.
e: Veera Simha Reddy is designed almost entirely as Balakrishna fan-service. Gopichand Malineni lands a few elevations and political punches, but the familiar dual-role structure, repetitive fights and underwhelming music leave the film without the content needed to make those highs memorable.
body:
Veera Simha Reddy once again reminded me of one thing: when it comes to combining huge Balakrishna elevations with genuinely strong mass content, Boyapati still understands that formula better than most.

Gopichand Malineni is himself a Balayya fan, and that affection is visible everywhere.

There are good elevation shots and a few political punches that will definitely excite the hardcore fan base.

But the film does not have enough fresh content underneath those moments.

The story follows an extremely familiar Balakrishna template: dual roles, the younger character largely existing in the shadow of the much more powerful senior character, and an elaborate backstory explaining the senior character’s conflict.

The sister sentiment tries to add an emotional layer, but even that reminded me of territory we have travelled through in earlier faction dramas.

Apart from the oora-mass fight in Istanbul, very little in the action felt new to me.

The movie has fight after fight, yet most of them use almost the same grammar — change the fighters, change the background, repeat the elevation 🙏

Thaman’s music and BGM were a massive asset in films such as Akhanda.

Here, they never gel with the material strongly enough to create the same impact.

The director’s intention is very clear: this movie is made primarily to serve the hardcore Balayya audience.

The funniest proof is probably having a major praise song called “Jai Balayya” when nobody inside the story is actually named Balayya or Balakrishna 🤣

Akhanda and Unstoppable had helped Balakrishna connect again with a wider set of younger and family audiences.

That is why I felt disappointed to see him return to such a familiar, narrowly fan-oriented subject.

The movie may still work commercially because of its mass format and festival timing.

But for me, it does not leave anything close to the impact created by Simha, Legend or Akhanda.
